title: Heterogeneous GPU latency envelopes and publish pipeline for model variants
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal: Produce a repeatable pipeline that authors, verifies, and publishes device-specific latency envelopes for model variants running on A100/H100/L40S/MI300 fleet flavors. The output is a signed 'envelope' artifact per (model,version,device-flavor) that captures expected latency percentiles (p50, p90, p95, p99), memory/KV footprint bands, and environmental tags (CUDA, driver, MIG config, container runtime). These envelopes will be consumed by rollout policies and the console to enable safe version pinning and automated fallback decisions.

Background and motivation: Current onboarding artifacts focus on single-point latency signatures and binary pass/fail gates. That representation hides multi-modality in latency distributions across heterogeneous hardware and runtime contexts. We need richer, probabilistic envelopes so routing and autoscaler logic can reason about tail risk and make informed tradeoffs (e.g., prefer lower-cost variant only when p99 within SLO).

Scope and deliverables:
- Data collection harness to run short microbench and production-sampled probes per device flavor (A100, H100, L40S, MI300).
- Envelope generation service (batch job) that computes percentile bands, interquartile ranges, and an uncertainty score.
- Metadata manifest format: flat JSON keys for consumption by console, router, and model-catalog. Manifest versioned with semver and signed with the publishing job id.
- Publisher that writes envelope artifacts to the model catalog and triggers a Catalog Index update.
- Monitoring and regression alerts: drift detector that emits ALERT-ENVELOPE-DRIFT when p95 shifts > 15% over a rolling 7-day baseline.
- Acceptance criteria: published envelopes exist for four target device flavors for the sample model (e.g., llama-2-13b), envelopes include p50/p90/p95/p99 and memory bands, unit test coverage of envelope generator, end-to-end smoke validation via canary rollout that adheres to SLOs.

Methodology details:
- Microbench suite: fixed prompt corpus (representative token lengths 16/64/256), 30-minute warmup, 1000 sequential online-like requests per device flavor. Collect per-token and per-request latencies, and KV cache warm/cold markers.
- Production sampling: lightweight telemetry trace sampling (0.5% of live requests) annotated with node SKU and driver versions to capture real-world distributional shifts.
- Envelope construction: compute empirical percentiles and then apply a Bayesian shrinkage estimator to produce an uncertainty score for each percentile; embed a "confidence_band" value to indicate narrow/wide envelopes.
- Environmental tags: CUDA version, driver build, container runtime, MIG config, and kernel path are included so differences are attributable.

Publishing contract and format (high level):
- artifact id: model:version:flavor:envelope:v{semver}

2025-02-25 - Design review with PM (Maya Singh) and runtime lead (Derek Wu). Agreed on shrinkage estimator approach and need for production sampling. Action: Noah to prototype generator and provide sample manifest by 2025-03-04.
2025-03-01 - Prototype generator v0.1 PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4923. Early feedback from infra: include driver and container tags to avoid noisy deltas from OS upgrades.
2025-03-03 - Blocker identified: our trace sampler doesn't yet record MIG config for L40S nodes. Blocking data completeness for L40S envelopes. Owner: infra team (see dependency ENG-120524).

2025-03-05 - Conversation with Console team (Sofia Ramos): manifest must be mappable to console's existing rollout UI; added flat fields p50,p90,p95,p99, memory_min_mb,memory_max_mb,confidence_band,source_sha. Will add compatibility shim in publisher.
2025-03-05 - Next steps: finish L40S sampling fix, iterate on PR to include signed manifest, add unit tests for envelope generator, schedule canary run for runtime-1.22 CI lane.
